pairs.locus: Albert of Aix, Historia Hierosolymitanae Expeditionis 5.9
pairs.question: Cur per aves haec fiant nuntia?
pairs.answer: Sed hac de causa praemissae sunt, ut rapido et incessabili volatu legationem fidei, quam erga eum habes, accelerent, et de auxilio tuo certificent, qualiscunque nobis in via fortuna vel impedimentum occurrerit.
pairs.derivation: After the duke and his men wonder at the release of the doves ('Dux et universi... de hac avium emissione mirantur'), the narrative poses the interrogative 'cur per aves haec fiant nuntia' (capitalized and given a question mark), which the legates explicitly answer ('illis a legatis responsum est'). The answer skips the non-answering preamble ('Non dominus noster dux, ejusque fideles super emissis mirentur columbis, quas non pueriliter, non frustra, praemisimus' = a deflection telling them not to wonder) and begins at the operative answering clause 'sed hac de causa praemissae sunt...' which states the reason (the birds speed the message of the pledged aid). It stops at the first full stop after 'occurrerit', before the legates add a second reason ('Est et aliud quare hae aves cum chartulis praemittuntur...'). The framing tag and the indirect-question wording in the narration were treated as framing; the section marker [0517D] falls outside the quoted spans.
